stem:
Two capacitors A and B are connected into the circuit shown in Fig. 5.1.

[[fig:f1]]

Capacitor A has capacitance *C* and capacitor B has capacitance 3*C*.
The electromotive force (e.m.f.) of the cell is *V*.
The two-way switch S is initially at position X, and capacitor B is initially uncharged.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.lead: State, in terms of *V* and *C*, expressions for:
parts.text: the initial charge *Q*ₐ on the plates of capacitor A

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: the initial energy *E*ₐ stored in capacitor A.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead: The two-way switch S is now moved to position Y.
parts.text: State and explain what happens to the charge that was initially on the plates of capacitor A.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
Show that the final potential difference (p.d.) *V*ᵦ across capacitor B is given by

*V*ᵦ = *V*/4.

Explain your reasoning.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Determine an expression, in terms of *V* and *C*, for the decrease Δ*E* in the total energy that is stored in the capacitors as a result of the change of the position of the switch.

figures.caption: Fig. 5.1
figures.alt: A circuit diagram showing a cell, capacitors A and B, and a two-way switch S with positions X and Y.
